parsed.rationale: Both `DiscogsMarkupParser.ResolvedToken` (line 89, `DiscogsMarkupParser.swift`) and `ResolvedBioToken` (line 20, `ResolvedBioToken.swift`) are `type-alias-union` declarations in the `Metadata` package with `shared_field_count: 9` and `differing_slots: null`, meaning they are exact duplicates. Maintaining two names for the same union type creates confusion about which alias to use and risks the two drifting apart if the union is ever extended. Neither record carries any test, codegen, mock, or sample-app flag, so the duplication is not intentional by policy. The standalone file `ResolvedBioToken.swift` signals that `ResolvedBioToken` was intended as the primary, public-facing name, making `DiscogsMarkupParser.ResolvedToken` the redundant alias to remove.

specifics.proposed_action: Determine which of the two type aliases is the canonical definition and delete the other, updating all call sites to use the surviving name. Given that `ResolvedBioToken` lives in its own dedicated file (`ResolvedBioToken.swift`) and has a top-level, non-nested name, it is the better candidate to keep. `DiscogsMarkupParser.ResolvedToken` (line 89 of `DiscogsMarkupParser.swift`) should be removed and replaced with a plain `typealias ResolvedToken = ResolvedBioToken` inside `DiscogsMarkupParser` if the nested name is still needed for readability, or removed entirely if it is not referenced outside the parser.
specifics.why_no_category_fits: Both records are `type-alias-union` declarations in the same package (`Metadata`) with 9 shared fields and no differing slots — they are structurally identical aliases for the same union type. The appropriate fix is not extraction (they are already in the same package), not a protocol/generic change, and not a macro. It is simply deduplication by deleting one alias and canonicalising on the other, which is a rename/delete operation that none of the named categories capture precisely.
